messages.author: c78bfd9857351762
messages.subject: Non-European reference population
parts:
I wanted to run a replication using non-European GWASs - not an admixed common factor model - but the same non-European population across traits.  

Would you be able to point me in the right direction for a non-European reference file for munging and mv ldsc.

Thanks!

messages.author: 3cd246d2b547f564
messages.subject: Re: Non-European reference population
parts: Pan UKBB has LDSC reference files for several ancestries groups: https://pan.ukbb.broadinstitute.org/downloads

On Friday, June 3, 2022 at 5:44:02 AM UTC+1 Daniel Rosoff wrote:
I wanted to run a replication using non-European GWASs - not an admixed common factor model - but the same non-European population across traits.  

Would you be able to point me in the right direction for a non-European reference file for munging and mv ldsc.

Thanks!

messages.author: c78bfd9857351762
messages.subject: Re: Non-European reference population
parts:
Thanks!  Two more questions:

1.The pan.ukbb LDSC-compatible flat files are chromosome combined.  Does GSEM look for 22 separate files for LDSC?  I would separate the chromosomes to make my folder look like eur_w_ld_chr?

2. Also, the LDSC github says CM (genetic position in cm) can be safely set to 0.  CM is not provided in the pan.ukbb LDSC-compatible flat files, nor is MAF.  Does GSEM use the CM? or MAF?

(Also, I also needed a 1000G population specific reference file; I downloaded the 1000GP_Phase3_Combined_Legend and cleaned it up (McCarthy Group Tools)).  .  

Dan

messages.author: 3b39745f73eec779
messages.subject: Re: Non-European reference population
parts:
1. You could split or try and set the chromosome argument (default chr = 22) to 1 and name the one file 1.l2.ldscore.gz which i think is the hardcoded filename extension it expects (perhaps that's something we want to change).

2. We don't use CM in any way as far as I am aware.

Best,
Michel
